papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category: detection — Contamination Detection Methods
  # ============================================================

  - id: "zhang_2024_minkpp"
    title: "Min-K%++: Improved Baseline for Detecting Pre-Training Data from Large Language Models"
    authors: "Zhang et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2025"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02936"
    category: "detection"
    role: "method-component"
    relevance: "Our S2 signal. Min-K%++ normalizes token probability with vocabulary statistics for membership inference. We discover its directional reversal at small model scales (Cohen's d = -1.2 to -2.7 at 0.5B d100) — a novel finding that challenges single-signal reliance."
    key_findings: "Theoretically motivated detection via normalized token probabilities; outperforms Min-K% on WikiMIA and other benchmarks."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal reveals Min-K++ is actively misleading (not just ineffective) at small scales — directional reversal is our headline empirical finding."

  - id: "shi_2023_minkprob"
    title: "Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models"
    authors: "Shi et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16789"
    category: "detection"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Original Min-K% Prob method and WikiMIA benchmark. Foundation for membership inference in LLMs. Min-K%++ (our S2) is a direct extension."
    key_findings: "Unseen examples have outlier low-probability tokens; Min-K% uses this for pretraining data detection without reference model."
    our_advantage: "We use the improved Min-K%++ variant and expose its failure modes at small scales."

  - id: "dekoninck_2024_constat"
    title: "ConStat: Performance-Based Contamination Detection in Large Language Models"
    authors: "Dekoninck et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16281"
    category: "detection"
    role: "method-component"
    relevance: "Our S3 signal candidate (excluded from final pipeline). Detects contamination as non-generalizing inflated performance by comparing primary vs reference benchmark performance against reference models."
    key_findings: "Novel contamination definition as non-generalizing performance inflation; detects contamination in Mistral, Llama, Yi, and top Open LLM Leaderboard models."
    our_advantage: "ConStat requires reference benchmarks and reference models; ContamCal integrates detection signals directly into IRT framework for calibrated score adjustment, not just detection."

  - id: "dong_2024_cdd"
    title: "Generalization or Memorization: Data Contamination and Trustworthy Evaluation for Large Language Models"
    authors: "Dong et al."
    venue: "ACL 2024 Findings"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15938"
    category: "detection"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Proposes CDD (output distribution peakedness) and TED (distribution correction for trustworthy evaluation). TED is closest to calibration but lacks IRT grounding and uncertainty quantification."
    key_findings: "CDD achieves 21-30% improvement over baselines in detection accuracy; TED mitigates up to 66.9% of contamination-attributed performance gain."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal provides full uncertainty quantification via Bayesian IRT posteriors; TED offers point corrections without credible intervals or identifiability analysis."

  - id: "zhang_2024_gsm1k"
    title: "A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic"
    authors: "Zhang et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00332"
    category: "detection"
    role: "method-component"
    relevance: "Our S4 signal (self-critique / GSM1k). Creates GSM1k to mirror GSM8k and measures accuracy drop as contamination proxy. Up to 13% accuracy drops in some model families."
    key_findings: "Systematic overfitting in Phi and Mistral families; positive correlation (r^2=0.32) between generation probability of GSM8k examples and performance gap."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal uses the GSM1k-style signal as one input to multi-signal RRF, then feeds into IRT for calibrated estimates rather than just flagging contamination."

  - id: "choi_2025_kds"
    title: "How Contaminated Is Your Benchmark? Quantifying Dataset Leakage in Large Language Models with Kernel Divergence"
    authors: "Choi et al."
    venue: "ICML 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00678"
    category: "detection"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "Kernel Divergence Score (KDS) detects contamination via embedding shift before/after fine-tuning. Near-perfect correlation with contamination levels. Complementary signal approach to our S1 embedding similarity."
    key_findings: "KDS captures fine-tuning-induced shifts in sample embeddings; outperforms existing baselines with near-perfect contamination level correlation."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal bridges detection to calibration; KDS only detects. Our S1 embedding similarity achieves AUC>0.95 without requiring fine-tuning comparison."

  - id: "oren_2023_proving_contamination"
    title: "Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models"
    authors: "Oren et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17623"
    category: "detection"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Provable contamination detection via exchangeability test on benchmark ordering likelihood. Complementary black-box approach."
    key_findings: "Detects contamination in models as small as 1.4B with 1000 examples; audits 5 popular LLMs finding little pervasive contamination."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal goes beyond detection to calibrated score adjustment with uncertainty quantification."

  - id: "deng_2024_tsguessing"
    title: "Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models"
    authors: "Deng, Zhao, Tang, Gerstein, & Cohan"
    year: 2024
    venue: "NAACL 2024"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09783"
    category: "detection"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "TS-Guessing protocol masks MC wrong options for fill-in; ChatGPT/GPT-4 guess correct options at 52%/57% on MMLU. Direct evidence that MC format is more vulnerable to contamination, supporting our finding that ARC (MC) shows γ>0 while GSM8K (generative) shows γ≈0."
    key_findings:
      - "MC format enables contaminated models to exploit memorized answer options"
      - "ChatGPT/GPT-4 MMLU option guessing rate 52%/57% vs random baseline"
      - "Open-ended format harder to game via memorization"

  - id: "schaeffer_2026_generative_contamination"
    title: "Quantifying the Effect of Test Set Contamination on Generative Evaluations"
    authors: "Schaeffer, Kazdan, Abbasi, Liu, et al."
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv 2026"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04301"
    category: "detection"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "First scaling law study of contamination on generative benchmarks (MATH). Even 1 test set replica in pretraining breaks irreducible error floor, but effect size much smaller than MC benchmarks. Consistent with our framework: generative γ expected smaller but non-zero."
    key_findings:
      - "Single test set replica in pretraining corpus breaks irreducible error on MATH"
      - "Contamination effect on generative benchmarks weaker than MC benchmarks"
      - "Scaling law characterization of contamination-performance relationship"

  # ============================================================
  # Category: irt-llm — IRT for LLM Evaluation
  # ============================================================

  - id: "lalor_2024_irt_nlp"
    title: "Item Response Theory for Natural Language Processing"
    authors: "Lalor et al."
    venue: "EACL 2024 Tutorial"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-tutorials.2/"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Comprehensive tutorial introducing IRT to NLP community. Establishes framework for psychometric LLM evaluation that ContamCal extends with contamination covariates."
    key_findings: "Demonstrates IRT benefits for NLP evaluation including difficulty estimation, benchmark quality assessment, and latent trait modeling."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal extends standard IRT with contamination covariate gamma, measurement error model, and per-benchmark effect estimation."

  - id: "polo_2024_tinybenchmarks"
    title: "tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples"
    authors: "Polo et al."
    venue: "ICML 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14992"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Uses IRT as performance estimator; 100 curated examples sufficient for MMLU. Demonstrates IRT scalability for LLM evaluation. Shares our assumption that IRT item parameters transfer across models."
    key_findings: "Accurate performance estimation with ~100 items per benchmark; IRT-based selection outperforms random subsampling."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal addresses a different problem: not efficiency but decontamination. We use IRT to model contamination effects rather than to reduce evaluation cost."

  - id: "habba_2025_growing_pains"
    title: "Growing Pains: Extensible and Efficient LLM Benchmarking Via Fixed Parameter Calibration"
    authors: "Habba et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12843"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Multidimensional IRT with anchor items for cross-study comparability. Addresses N insufficiency via fixed parameter calibration. Directly relevant to our N>=50 identifiability concern."
    key_findings: "Predicts full-evaluation performance within 2-3pp using 100 anchor items; Spearman rho>=0.9 across 400+ models."
    our_advantage: "Growing Pains assumes no contamination; ContamCal explicitly models contamination effects. Their anchor-item framework could complement our decontamination pipeline."

  - id: "luettgau_2025_hibayes"
    title: "HiBayES: A Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling Framework for AI Evaluation Statistics"
    authors: "Luettgau et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05602"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Hierarchical Bayesian framework for LLM evaluation with principled UQ, especially in low-data scenarios (<20 data points). Does not model contamination. Most methodologically similar to ContamCal's Bayesian approach."
    key_findings: "Robust parameter estimation via hierarchical GLMs with formal model comparison; handles nested evaluation structures."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal adds contamination-specific covariates (gamma_k, exposure scores) to the Bayesian framework. HiBayES provides UQ but ignores contamination effects entirely."

  - id: "li_2024_atlas"
    title: "Adaptive Testing for LLM Evaluation: A Psychometric Alternative to Static Benchmarks"
    authors: "Li et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.04689"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "ATLAS uses Fisher information-guided adaptive item selection for efficient LLM evaluation with up to 90% item reduction. Validates IRT psychometric framework for LLM evaluation."
    key_findings: "30-89 items per benchmark sufficient with SE-controlled stopping; best accuracy-efficiency tradeoff among IRT-based methods."
    our_advantage: "ATLAS optimizes evaluation efficiency; ContamCal addresses evaluation validity under contamination. Complementary goals."

  - id: "zhou_2025_psnirt"
    title: "Lost in Benchmarks? Rethinking Large Language Model Benchmarking with Item Response Theory"
    authors: "Zhou et al."
    venue: "AAAI 2026"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15055"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "PSN-IRT uses pseudo-siamese networks for rich item parameter estimation. Analyzes 11 benchmarks (41,871 items) revealing measurement quality shortcomings."
    key_findings: "LLM benchmarks suffer widespread saturation and insufficient difficulty ceilings; PSN-IRT constructs smaller benchmarks with stronger human preference alignment."
    our_advantage: "PSN-IRT diagnoses benchmark quality; ContamCal diagnoses and corrects contamination effects. Our gamma_k captures a specific quality dimension (data leakage) that PSN-IRT does not model."

  - id: "burnell_2023_structure"
    title: "Revealing the structure of language model capabilities"
    authors: "Burnell et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10062"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Factor analysis reveals 3 capability dimensions (reasoning, comprehension, core language modeling) in LLMs. Supports multidimensional view; our unidimensional theta per benchmark is acknowledged as simplification in Limitations."
    key_findings: "LLM capabilities are not monolithic; 3 factors explain high proportion of performance variance across 29 LLMs on 27 tasks."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal's unidimensional theta per benchmark is a deliberate simplification acknowledged in Limitations; multidimensional extension is future work."

  - id: "brown_2024_ppp"
    title: "The Expected Behaviors of Posterior Predictive Tests and Their Unexpected Interpretation"
    authors: "Brown & Thomson"
    year: 2024
    venue: "Molecular Biology and Evolution, 41(3), msae051"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Proves PPP distribution is inherently non-uniform (unlike frequentist p-values), concentrated near 0.5. Extreme PPP (e.g. our 0.003) provides stronger poor-fit evidence than usually assumed, but low PPP does not automatically invalidate parameter estimates — supports our position that γ posterior excluding zero remains informative even with poor global fit."
    key_findings:
      - "PPP distribution is non-uniform, concentrated around 0.5"
      - "Low PPP does not automatically negate parameter estimate informativeness"
      - "Posterior predictive tests evaluate models under favorable conditions (model already fitted to data)"

  - id: "sinharay_2025_irt_fit"
    title: "Assessment of Fit of Item Response Theory Models: A Critical Review of the Status Quo and Some Future Directions"
    authors: "Sinharay, S."
    year: 2025
    venue: "British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 78, 711–733"
    category: "irt-llm"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Comprehensive review of IRT model fit assessment (PPMC, generalized residuals, person-fit). Argues low PPP indicates model inadequacy but not that parameter estimates are meaningless. Supports our ARC PPP=0.003 but γ still interpretable position."
    key_findings:
      - "PPP interpretation requires caution — low PPP means model inadequacy, not parameter invalidity"
      - "Covers PPMC, generalized residuals, person-fit diagnostics"
      - "Authoritative 2025 review likely known to reviewers"

  # ============================================================
  # Category: item-compromise — Educational Measurement
  # ============================================================

  - id: "eckerly_2017_item_compromise"
    title: "Detecting preknowledge and item compromise: Understanding the status quo"
    authors: "Eckerly, C."
    venue: "Handbook of Quantitative Methods for Detecting Cheating on Tests (Routledge)"
    year: 2017
    url: "https://www.routledge.com/9781138821811"
    category: "item-compromise"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Core theoretical foundation for ContamCal. Reviews IRT methods for detecting compromised items and examinees with preknowledge. Our gamma parameter directly extends the item compromise framework to LLM benchmark contamination."
    key_findings: "Systematic framework for item preknowledge detection using IRT-based person-fit statistics and item parameter drift."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal adapts item compromise IRT from human testing to LLM evaluation with 3 structural adaptations: independent examinees -> single model, binary leakage -> continuous exposure, stable ability -> regime-conditional ability."
    verified: false

  - id: "sinharay_2017_preknowledge"
    title: "Detection of item preknowledge using likelihood ratio test and score test"
    authors: "Sinharay, S."
    venue: "Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 42(1)"
    year: 2017
    url: "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29881099/"
    category: "item-compromise"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Proposes LRT-based statistics for item preknowledge detection with known Type I error rates. Our treatment of contamination-induced item parameter drift builds on this work."
    key_findings: "LRT statistic for item preknowledge has similar power to posterior shift statistic with known null distribution; applicable to adaptive and non-adaptive tests."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal extends from binary preknowledge to continuous contamination exposure scores and from human examinees to LLM respondents."

  - id: "deboeck_2004_explanatory_irt"
    title: "Explanatory Item Response Models: A Generalized Linear and Nonlinear Approach"
    authors: "De Boeck, P. & Wilson, M."
    venue: "Springer"
    year: 2004
    url: "https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-3990-9"
    category: "item-compromise"
    role: "foundation"
    relevance: "Foundational text for explanatory IRT. ContamCal's contamination-augmented 4PL is an explanatory IRT model where item responses are modeled as a function of contamination exposure predictors."
    key_findings: "Unifies IRT with generalized linear/nonlinear mixed models; enables item covariates (like our exposure scores) as predictors in IRT framework."
    our_advantage: "Direct theoretical grounding. ContamCal instantiates the explanatory IRT framework with contamination-specific covariates."

  - id: "kievit_2013_simpsons_paradox"
    title: "Simpson's Paradox in Psychological Science: A Practical Guide"
    authors: "Kievit, Frankenhuis, Waldorp, & Borsboom"
    year: 2013
    venue: "Frontiers in Psychology, 4, 513"
    category: "item-compromise"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Theoretical framework for Simpson's paradox in behavioral science. Directly applicable to our MMLU finding: pooled γ insignificant but domain-level analysis reveals significant positive and negative γ that cancel upon aggregation."
    key_findings:
      - "Simpson's paradox more prevalent in psychology than traditionally recognized"
      - "Effect direction can reverse when moving from population to subgroup (or vice versa)"
      - "Provides statistical markers and R detection toolkit"

  - id: "ercikan_2008_dif_cancellation"
    title: "Differential Item Functioning Amplification and Cancellation in a Reading Test"
    authors: "Ercikan, Arim, & Oliveri"
    year: 2008
    venue: "Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 14(3)"
    category: "item-compromise"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Empirical precedent for DIF cancellation: most items show significant DIF but favoring different groups, so DIF cancels at total test score level. Direct analogue to our MMLU domain-level contamination signals with inconsistent directions being masked in pooled analysis."
    key_findings:
      - "Majority of items show significant DIF but in opposing directions"
      - "DIF cancels at aggregate test score level despite item-level significance"
      - "Multiple-group testlet IRT model reveals hidden heterogeneity"

  # ============================================================
  # Category: calibration — Calibration & Score Adjustment
  # ============================================================

  - id: "xu_2025_dcr"
    title: "DCR: Quantifying Data Contamination in LLMs Evaluation"
    authors: "Xu et al."
    venue: "EMNLP 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11405"
    category: "calibration"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Only existing method producing adjusted accuracy via fuzzy inference. ContamCal's primary competitor. DCR quantifies contamination risk across 4 levels (semantic, informational, data, label) and adjusts raw accuracy."
    key_findings: "DCR Factor adjusts accuracy within 4% average error across 3 benchmarks; validated on 0.5B-72B models."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal provides Bayesian credible intervals (DCR gives point estimates only), per-benchmark gamma_k characterization, and IRT-grounded identifiability analysis. DCR lacks UQ and theoretical identifiability bounds."

  - id: "guo_2017_calibration"
    title: "On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks"
    authors: "Guo et al."
    venue: "ICML 2017"
    year: 2017
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599"
    category: "calibration"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Foundational work on probability calibration in neural networks. Must disambiguate: our 'calibration' means decontamination score adjustment, not probability calibration (confidence = accuracy). Temperature scaling is unrelated to our method."
    key_findings: "Modern neural networks are poorly calibrated; temperature scaling (single parameter) effectively recalibrates predictions."
    our_advantage: "Different notion of calibration. Guo et al. calibrate prediction confidence; ContamCal calibrates benchmark scores for contamination effects."

  - id: "angelopoulos_2023_conformal"
    title: "A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification"
    authors: "Angelopoulos & Bates"
    venue: "Foundations and Trends in ML, 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511"
    category: "calibration"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Alternative UQ approach with distribution-free coverage guarantees. Discussed in Related Work to justify why Bayesian IRT is preferred over conformal for our setting (conformal requires exchangeability assumptions violated by contamination structure)."
    key_findings: "Conformal prediction provides statistically rigorous uncertainty sets without distributional assumptions; applicable to any pre-trained model."
    our_advantage: "Bayesian IRT provides interpretable per-item parameters and contamination-specific covariates; conformal gives coverage guarantees but no mechanistic insight into contamination effects."

  # Category: mitigation — Contamination Mitigation & Alternatives
  # ============================================================

  - id: "sun_2025_emperors_new_clothes"
    title: "The Emperor's New Clothes in Benchmarking? A Rigorous Examination of Mitigation Strategies for LLM Benchmark Data Contamination"
    authors: "Sun et al."
    venue: "ICML 2025"
    year: 2025
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16402"
    category: "mitigation"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Demonstrates all 20 existing mitigation strategies fail to balance fidelity and contamination resistance across all benchmarks. Strongest motivation for ContamCal's post-hoc calibration approach."
    key_findings: "No semantic-preserving strategy significantly improves resistance over vanilla; semantic-altering strategies sacrifice fidelity. 10 LLMs x 5 benchmarks x 20 strategies x 2 scenarios."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal offers post-hoc calibration rather than prevention — complementary approach. Emperor's failure motivates calibration; ContamCal provides it."

  - id: "white_2024_livebench"
    title: "LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark"
    authors: "White et al."
    venue: "arXiv 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19314"
    category: "mitigation"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "Dynamic benchmark alternative: monthly-updated questions from recent sources to prevent contamination. Complementary to ContamCal — LiveBench prevents contamination for new evaluations; ContamCal calibrates existing contaminated benchmarks."
    key_findings: "Top models achieve below 70% accuracy; monthly updates with 18 tasks across 6 categories maintain contamination resistance."
    our_advantage: "LiveBench requires continuous curation; ContamCal works with existing static benchmarks. Both valid approaches to the contamination problem."

  # Category: benchmark — Evaluation Frameworks & Alternatives
  # ============================================================

  - id: "liang_2023_helm"
    title: "Holistic Evaluation of Language Models"
    authors: "Liang et al."
    venue: "TMLR 2023"
    year: 2023
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09110"
    category: "benchmark"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "HELM evaluates 30 models on 42 scenarios with 7 metrics including calibration. Establishes standardized evaluation framework. ContamCal addresses a gap HELM does not: score reliability under contamination."
    key_findings: "Prior to HELM, models were evaluated on only 17.9% of core scenarios; standardized evaluation reveals 25 top-level findings across models."
    our_advantage: "HELM assumes benchmark scores are trustworthy; ContamCal questions and corrects this assumption when contamination is present."

  - id: "chiang_2024_chatbot_arena"
    title: "Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference"
    authors: "Chiang et al."
    venue: "ICML 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04132"
    category: "benchmark"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Human pairwise comparison evaluation that inherently bypasses benchmark contamination. Discussed as contamination-resistant alternative."
    key_findings: "240K+ votes via crowdsourced pairwise comparisons; Elo rating system for model ranking without static test sets."
    our_advantage: "Chatbot Arena requires human judges and live interaction; ContamCal enables post-hoc calibration of automated benchmark scores, which scale better."

  - id: "li_2024_open_llm_leaderboard"
    title: "Open-LLM-Leaderboard: From Multi-choice to Open-style Questions for LLMs Evaluation, Benchmark, and Arena"
    authors: "Li et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2024"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07545"
    category: "benchmark"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "Converting MC benchmarks to open-style questions causes ~25% average accuracy drop across all models. Quantifies MC format advantage (selection bias, random guessing) that amplifies contamination signal in MC benchmarks. Supports our MC/generative format as contamination effect moderator."
    key_findings:

# Figures and Tables Analysis

## Total Count
The document contains **4 main figures** and **8 main tables** (plus additional tables in appendices).

## Key Figures

**Figure 1**: Shows benchmark data contamination mitigation strategies, illustrating how methods like synonym replacement and analysis extension update benchmark questions to reduce direct memorization risks.

**Figure 2**: Demonstrates limitations of existing assessment approaches. The graphic shows how accuracy drop and accuracy matching metrics fail to capture question-level mismatches—models may match aggregate accuracy while answering different specific questions correctly.

**Figure 4**: A scatter plot visualization comparing fidelity (x-axis) versus contamination resistance (y-axis) across different mitigation strategies under mild and intensive contamination. Single strategies appear in blue, combined strategies in yellow, and the vanilla baseline in red. The ideal outcome would occupy the upper-right quadrant, but no strategy achieves this balance.

## Table Structures

**Table 3**: Presents fidelity and resistance metrics for 16 semantic-preserving strategies across 5 benchmarks. Each value represents the average of 10 LLM scores. Green highlighting indicates statistically significant resistance improvements over vanilla.

**Table 4**: Covers 4 semantic-altering mitigation strategies on Arc-C and MMLU only, showing these approaches achieve higher resistance but at the cost of notably reduced fidelity scores.

## Content Distribution

**Main paper**: Focuses on core methodology, results presentation, and key findings from experiments spanning 10 LLMs, 5 benchmarks, and 20 mitigation strategies.

**Appendices**: Contain extended related work on detection methods, comprehensive pipeline implementation details, fine-tuning recipes, contamination effectiveness metrics, and complete detection results across all candidate models.
